context_documents.purpose: Project's standing conventions for language, errors and testing.

tasks.objective: A caller can reserve a seat for a preloaded event before it starts, and unknown or started events are refused, all under a test-controlled clock.
completion_criteria: With a controlled time one second before the start instant, reserving for an event with free seats returns an active reservation with a new ID and the supplied event and attendee IDs.
Reserving for an unknown event returns EVENT_NOT_FOUND and leaves the set of reservations and free seats unchanged.

Reserving at exactly the start instant and one second after it returns EVENT_STARTED, creates no reservation and consumes no seat; reserving one second before the start still succeeds on the same event.
All checks run locally by setting the controlled time directly, with no sleeps, wall-clock reads or network.
constraints: Current time must come only from a time source the test can set; events are preloaded with an ID, positive capacity and UTC start instant.

tasks.objective: Capacity and duplicate rules hold for sequential calls: a full event refuses new attendees while an active attendee can safely retry.
completion_criteria: On an event with capacity 1 holding one active reservation, a different attendee receives CAPACITY_EXCEEDED, no reservation is added and the existing reservation is unchanged.
Retrying for an attendee who already has an active reservation returns the same reservation ID and active state, including when the event is full.
On an event with capacity 2, a retry by the first attendee consumes no extra seat: a second attendee still succeeds and a third receives CAPACITY_EXCEEDED.
At and after the start instant, a retry for an attendee with an active reservation returns EVENT_STARTED instead of the existing reservation, and the reservation stays active and unchanged.

tasks.objective: Simultaneous attempts cannot oversell the last seat or create two active reservations for one attendee, and this is demonstrated deterministically.
completion_criteria: With one seat left, simultaneous attempts by two different attendees yield exactly one success and one CAPACITY_EXCEEDED, and active reservations never exceed capacity.
Simultaneous duplicate requests by one attendee for one event all return the same reservation ID and together occupy exactly one seat.
The checks force overlapping calls through a reproducible, deterministic interleaving and are repeated across several interleavings, with no sleeps, timing assumptions or network.
constraints: The capacity check, duplicate check and creation of the reservation must behave as one indivisible step with respect to other calls.

tasks.objective: A caller can cancel an active reservation before the event starts, which releases exactly one seat; repeats and unknown IDs are handled safely.
completion_criteria: On a full event with capacity 2, cancelling one active reservation returns the same ID in cancelled state, then a different attendee can immediately reserve and the next new attendee receives CAPACITY_EXCEEDED, showing exactly one seat was released.
Repeating the cancellation before the start returns the same ID in cancelled state and releases no additional seat: a further new attendee still receives CAPACITY_EXCEEDED.
Cancelling an unknown reservation ID returns RESERVATION_NOT_FOUND and leaves all reservations and free seats unchanged.

tasks.objective: An attendee whose reservation was cancelled can book again and receives a fresh reservation while the old one stays cancelled.
completion_criteria: After cancelling, the original attendee reserving the same event before the start receives an active reservation whose ID differs from the cancelled one.
Inspecting the earlier reservation afterwards shows it is still cancelled, and a further reserve by the attendee returns the fresh ID, not the cancelled one.
When the event is full after cancellation, the original attendee rebooking receives CAPACITY_EXCEEDED and no reservation is added.

tasks.objective: Cancellation at or after the event start is refused for active reservations, remains idempotent for cancelled ones, and still reports unknown IDs.
completion_criteria: At exactly the start instant and one second after it, cancelling an active reservation returns EVENT_STARTED, the reservation stays active and the occupied seat count is unchanged.
One second before the start instant, cancelling the same kind of active reservation still succeeds.
Retrying the cancellation of an already cancelled reservation at and after the start returns the same ID in cancelled state with no capacity effect.
Cancelling an unknown ID at and after the start returns RESERVATION_NOT_FOUND with no state change.

tasks.objective: Every success state and error code is distinguishable and every failure is shown not to change reservation or capacity state.
completion_criteria: A table of failing calls covering EVENT_NOT_FOUND, EVENT_STARTED, CAPACITY_EXCEEDED and RESERVATION_NOT_FOUND for both reserve and cancel shows each returns its own stable code.
For each failing call, the reservation records and free seats observed through the test inspection are identical before and after the call.
The whole suite runs locally using only the controlled time source and deterministic concurrency checks, with no sleeps, network or external services.
